episode: Two Bathroom Remodel, The Copper House
assessment: Two bathrooms in one episode and an angle the others have not had: the homeowner designed the whole thing herself in SketchUp, picked every finish and ordered all of it, down to the tile layout her tile setter had to work from. That is the Short. The hammered copper tub is the signature image and it names the house. The reveal runs 11:32 to 15:48 plus a clean master bath wide at 17:34 to 18:00, so there is enough for one Short with a little spare. The walk in shower draft story at 14:16 to 15:16, where she tried it without a door and froze, is a genuinely good second Short on its own and is left out of this one for room.

project_context.summary: Two bathrooms in an older house. The master was expanded and got a hammered copper freestanding tub, French doors repurposed from the family room downstairs, a shower tiled to the homeowner's own random pattern in two tile sizes, a quartz bench top and a marble topped shower vent, and a sliding glass door replaced with a double casement window. The main bath was rearranged around the existing vanity, with a Euro door shower, a rain head and hand held, and a honeycomb tile floor.
project_context.segment_choice: One Short, cut from 11:32 to 15:48 and the clean master bath wide at 17:34. No before footage, no progress footage, and nothing from the labelled comparison montage after 18:03.
notes: Every frame is a finished bathroom.
The homeowner designed it, and the Short says so. That is the hook.

shorts.full_vo:
Two bathrooms done, and the homeowner designed both of them herself. That tub is hammered copper, with a freestanding filler beside it. The French doors came from the family room downstairs, repainted and put back up here.

The shower tile is her pattern, two sizes, and every row mapped out. My tile guy had to work off her drawings to set it. The bench top is quartz, and the controls are all black.

In the main bath, a Euro door, a rain head and a hand held. Her pattern again on the walls. And a honeycomb tile floor. The sliding glass door is now a double casement window.

She picked the mirrors, the sconces, the light fixtures, all of it. Her design, from the drawings to the last tile.
shorts.voice_direction: Warm and unhurried, a contractor showing a friend the finished rooms, and genuinely pleased to hand the credit to the homeowner.
